question: Should OpenClaw expose Discord bot presence mutation to plugins as a public runtime API, and what gate, account scoping, and precedence model should it use?
rationale: The implementation path exists internally, but promoting it to plugin runtime changes the public plugin contract and exposes a Discord bot-credential-backed mutation boundary to plugin code.

options.title: Design a gated runtime API
options.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence`-style runtime seam with explicit gating, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence rules.

options.title: Keep presence as message action only
options.body: Leave dynamic presence mutation on the existing default-off `setPresence` message action and document that plugins should not mutate Discord presence directly.

options.title: Fold into self-profile direction
options.body: Defer this request behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34004 if maintainers want one Discord identity/profile API instead of a separate presence-only runtime API.

recommendation.title: Design a gated runtime API
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence`-style runtime seam with explicit gating, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence rules.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily whether to reintroduce a Discord-specific plugin-runtime seam after the plugin-runtime boundary refactor.
